item.content:encoded: Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz hat mehrere EU-Staats- und Regierungschefs eingeladen, um sich in der laufenden Debatte um die künftigen EU-Finanzen abzusprechen. Es sei noch nicht klar, ob die Liste der Teilnehmer Dänemark, Österreich, Finnland und die Niederlande abschließend sei, sagte Regierungssprecher Stefan Kornelius am Montag in Berlin. Eingeladen seien Länder, die das Ziel teilten, dass der sogenannte EU-Finanzrahmen für die Jahre 2028 bis 2034 noch in diesem Jahr abgeschlossen werden solle. Es handelt sich zudem um Nettozahlerstaaten, also Länder, die mehr Geld nach Brüssel überweisen, als sie über Programme und Subventionen zurückbekommen. Frankreichs Präsident Emmanuel Macron werde nicht kommen, aber mit ihm habe Merz bereits eine sehr enge Abstimmung bei dem Thema. Kornelius verwies auf die Position des Kanzlers, dass der bisher vorliegende Budgetentwurf "in allen Bereichen, und zwar um mehrere hundert Milliarden Euro" gekürzt werden müsse. Die Regierung fordert ein Abspecken der EU-Kommissionsvorschläge von zwei Billionen Euro auf 1,6 Billionen Euro für die siebenjährige Periode. Man müsse sehen, wie weit man mit den neuen EU-Eigenmitteln komme, also eigenen Einnahmequellen der EU. Zudem müssten die neuen politischen Prioritäten im Finanzrahmen abgebildet werden. "Das ist der Rahmen, in dem auch verhandelt oder gesprochen wird", betonte Merz. Der Kanzler hatte darüber auch im Juli bei einem Besuch in Irland gesprochen, das derzeit die EU-Ratspräsidentschaft innehat und in dieser Funktion wahrscheinlich im Oktober ein neues Finanztableau vorlegen soll. Deutschland und Frankreich drängen auf einen Abschluss noch in diesem Jahr. Grund ist auch, dass wegen wichtiger Wahlen in Frankreich, Polen und Italien im kommenden Jahr kein Abschluss erwartet wird.

item.title: Miners support UK stocks as investors eye key events
item.description: The main UK stock indexes edged higher on Monday, as miners helped offset geopolitical tensions, while investors braced for big-ticket events that could set the tone for global markets in the near term.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The main UK stock indexes edged higher on Monday, as miners helped offset geopolitical tensions, while investors braced for big-ticket events that could set the tone for global markets in the near term. The blue-chip FTSE 100 index (.FTSE) rose 0.2% to 10,835.77 points by 1141 GMT, while the midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC) was flat at 24,725.18 points. Investors are awaiting [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"details "]on new U.S. sanctions targeting Iran's trade partners, which could disrupt crude supplies from the Middle East. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to hold a press conference later in the day to outline the sanctions. Washington says Iran must relinquish its control over the vital Strait of Hormuz, a route that once carried a fifth of global supplies. Oil prices , eased ahead of the announcement, dragging down British energy majors BP (BP.L) and Shell (SHEL.L) . On the flipside, miners Rio Tinto (RIO.L) and Anglo American (AAL.L) gained 0.6% and 2.2%, respectively, as a weaker U.S. currency supported metal prices. This week, investors will keep a close watch on chipmaker Nvidia's (NVDA.O) earnings, seen as a major test of the AI rally that has been a key driver of pushing stocks to record highs. U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's debut speech at the annual Jackson Hole conference this week will also be on traders' radar as they seek guidance about the recent jump in bond yields and monetary policy outlook. British distribution firm Diploma (DPLM.L) gained 1.5% after J.P.Morgan [USN:L6N44L0E4 TEXT:"raised"] its rating from neutral to outperform and increased price target to 8250 pence from 5760 pence. Shell (SHEL.L) has drawn interest from potential bidders, including ExxonMobil (XOM.N) and LyondellBasell (LYB.N) , for its U.S. chemical assets that could fetch up to $8 billion, the Financial Times reported. Shell's stock dipped in-line with oil prices. Shares of transport tech company Tracsis (TRCS.L) rose 7% after raising its full-year forecasts.

item.title: Roche, Eli Lilly's Alzheimer's blood test gets FDA clearance
item.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has cleared Roche and partner Eli Lilly's blood test to help identify signs of Alzheimer's disease in people aged 55 and older with cognitive decline.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has cleared Roche (ROPC.S) and partner Eli Lilly's (LLY.N) blood test to help identify signs of Alzheimer's disease in people aged 55 and older with cognitive decline. The test, Elecsys pTau217, is a biomarker blood test that can help doctors identify patients who are likely or unlikely to have Alzheimer's-related brain changes, Roche said on Monday. The FDA clearance follows European approval for the test in May. The test can be run on more than 4,500 Roche laboratory analyzers already installed across the United States, which the company said could help broaden access. Separately, Labcorp (LH.N) and Quest Diagnostics (DGX.N) said that they plan to offer the test through their laboratory networks, potentially expanding availability across the United States. Roche did not disclose the test's price. Current methods to detect amyloid, a protein linked to the disease, typically rely on positron emission tomography or PET scans or cerebrospinal fluid testing, which can be expensive, invasive and less widely available. The FDA clearance comes as drugmakers and diagnostic companies race to develop simpler tests for Alzheimer's disease amid growing demand for earlier diagnosis and treatment. [USN:L3N3VU0ZL TEXT:"Fujirebio's Lumipulse"] became the first blood test cleared by the FDA to aid in the assessment of Alzheimer's disease in 2025. Elecsys pTau217 is not intended to be used as a standalone diagnostic test and results should be interpreted alongside other clinical information, Roche said.

item.title: nVent Electric to buy Maverick Power for $1.75 billion to expand data center offerings
item.description: nVent Electric said on Monday it would acquire data center equipment maker Maverick Power for $1.75 billion as it looks to expand its presence in a booming AI infrastructure market.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: nVent Electric (NVT.N) said on Monday it would acquire data center equipment maker Maverick Power for $1.75 billion as it looks to expand its presence in a booming AI infrastructure market. Electrical equipment and systems suppliers like nVent have benefited as companies ramp up investment to support the rapid expansion of AI computing capacity, with CEO Beth Wozniak saying the Maverick acquisition will add power distribution capabilities and strengthen its offerings to data center customers. The deal also includes a potential additional consideration of up to $550 million in cash if Maverick achieves certain performance targets in 2027 and 2028, nVent said. McKinney, Texas-based Maverick Power makes engineered power distribution and infrastructure solutions, including low- and medium-voltage switchgears and switchboards, and integrated modular solutions. nVent expects to fund the deal with a combination of cash on hand and new debt. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approval. Shares of London-based nVent were down 1.3% in premarket trading.

item.title: Tunisian hospital receives 19 bodies after migrant boat sinks
item.description: A hospital in the southern Tunisian city of Ben Guerdane has received at least 19 bodies of migrants recovered from the sea over the past two days, the head of a migrant rights group said on Monday, following the sinking of a boat at the weekend.
item.dc:creator: Tarek Amara
item.content:encoded: A hospital in the southern Tunisian city of Ben Guerdane has received at least 19 bodies of migrants recovered from the sea over the past two days, the head of a migrant rights group said on Monday, following the sinking of a [USN:L1N44J00D TEXT:"boat"] at the weekend. The sinking of the migrant boat, which carried seven members of the same family, sparked a wave of grief and anger triggering violent protests in the city on Sunday night. Protesters burned tyres and blocked roads, while police responded by firing tear gas to disperse the crowds. Protesters are demanding better living conditions and economic development, saying a lack of opportunities and years of marginalisation are pushing young people to undertake dangerous sea crossings to Europe in search of a better life. It was not clear if all the bodies were from the boat that sank. Mostafa Abdelkebir, the head of the Tunisian Observatory for Human Rights, told Reuters that genetic testing was being carried out to identify the bodies and determine how many of them had been aboard the boat, while searches continued for other people who may still be missing. Tunisia was once a major departure point for migrants crossing the Mediterranean, but departures have fallen sharply over the past two years amid a crackdown and tighter maritime controls, backed by European funding and modern border-monitoring equipment, particularly from Italy. Human Rights Watch, Amnesty International and dozens of other human rights and humanitarian groups said in a statement last month that the EU-Tunisia migration deal had fuelled and normalised serious abuses against migrants and asylum seekers in Tunisia.

item.title: Dólar ronda mínimos de varios meses, mientras incertidumbre sobre deuda inquieta a inversores
item.description: El dólar cotizaba el lunes cerca de mínimos de varios meses, en un mercado inquieto por la promesa del Tesoro estadounidense de recomprar más bonos a largo plazo, mientras los operadores esperan detalles sobre las sanciones a Irán y los discursos sobre política monetaria de esta semana en Estados Unidos y Japón.
item.dc:creator: Tom Westbrook, Johann Cherian
item.content:encoded: El dólar cotizaba el lunes cerca de mínimos de varios meses, en un mercado inquieto por la promesa del Tesoro estadounidense de recomprar más bonos a largo plazo, mientras los operadores esperan detalles sobre las sanciones a Irán y los discursos sobre política monetaria de esta semana en Estados Unidos y Japón. * Las tensiones comerciales lastraban al dólar canadiense , que caía un 0,5%, a 1,384 unidades, frente a su par estadounidense, después de que Washington impusiera aranceles del 50% a los productos canadienses y Canadá respondiera con medidas similares. * El euro bajaba levemente a 1,1664 dólares, pero seguía cerca del máximo de tres meses alcanzado la semana pasada. * La libra esterlina también declinaba a 1,3627 dólares, pero continuaba rondando un pico de seis meses de 1,3675 dólares alcanzado también el viernes. El yen descendía a 159,21 unidades por dólar. * El billete verde registró el domingo su mayor caída semanal frente al bitcóin en casi tres años y medio, y ha estado cayendo con fuerza frente al oro debido al resurgimiento de los temores de que la moneda se vea afectada si Estados Unidos intenta contener el rendimiento de los bonos. * Los retornos a largo plazo han ido subiendo a nivel mundial debido a una combinación de sólidas perspectivas de crecimiento económico, crecientes expectativas de inflación y preocupación por el aumento desmesurado de la deuda soberana. * Después de que el rendimiento de las notas a 30 años alcanzara máximos de casi dos décadas, el Tesoro anunció la semana pasada que duplicaría las recompras de deuda a largo plazo hasta los 4.000 millones de dólares por operación. La cuantía es insignificante en un mercado valorado en 32 billones de dólares, pero la señal intervencionista asustó a los operadores y afectó al dólar. * "Cuanto más intente (el secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent) hacer frente a la situación, más se le opondrán los mercados", afirmó Marc Ostwald, de ADM Investor Services International. "Como resultado, veremos lo mismo que hemos observado la semana pasada: un fuerte apoyo al oro y al bitcóin".

item.title: Braskem entra com pedido de recuperação extrajudicial, dizem fontes

item.content:encoded: A petroquímica Braskem (BRKM3.SA) entrou com pedido de recuperação extrajudicial, disseram duas fontes a par do assunto nesta segunda-feira, enquanto lida com uma dívida superior a US$10 bilhões em suas operações no Brasil, na Europa e nos Estados Unidos. A medida ocorre depois que a Braskem Idesa, uma joint venture entre a empresa brasileira e o mexicano Grupo Idesa, ingressou com [USN:L1N44F0TB TEXT:"pedido de recuperação judicial"] (Chapter 11) nos EUA na semana passada. A posição de caixa da Braskem foi severamente afetada pelos preços baixos no setor petroquímico e por um desastre relacionado às suas minas de sal no Nordeste. A [USN:L1N4490ZZ TEXT:"Reuters noticiou"], no início deste mês, que a empresa estava em negociações avançadas para um potencial pedido de recuperação extrajudicial no Brasil antes do final de agosto, quando expiraria uma proteção emergencial de 60 dias, ao mesmo tempo em que explorava opções de reestruturação para sua subsidiária mexicana. A Braskem não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário. ((Por Luciana Magalhães, com reportagem adicional de Isabel Teles))

item.title: Ucrânia quer paz, mas não vai ceder, diz Zelenskiy no Dia da Independência
item.description: A Ucrânia quer a paz, mas não vai simplesmente ceder à Rússia a qualquer preço, afirmou o presidente Volodymyr Zelenskiy em um discurso desafiador na segunda-feira, enquanto líderes estrangeiros se reuniam em Kiev para as comemorações do Dia da Independência.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Anna Pruchnicka
item.content:encoded: A Ucrânia quer a paz, mas não vai simplesmente ceder à Rússia a qualquer preço, afirmou o presidente Volodymyr Zelenskiy em um discurso desafiador na segunda-feira, enquanto líderes estrangeiros se reuniam em Kiev para as comemorações do Dia da Independência. O primeiro-ministro britânico, Andy Burnham, e o presidente do Conselho Europeu, António Costa, estavam entre as autoridades estrangeiras presentes nas comemorações do 35º aniversário da separação da Ucrânia da União Soviética. Burnham, em sua primeira visita à capital ucraniana como primeiro-ministro, anunciaria o apoio britânico para ajudar Kiev a aumentar sua produção nacional de mísseis de longo alcance. Ele também tinha programado co-presidir uma reunião virtual da “Coalizão dos Dispostos” — um grupo de países que apoia a Ucrânia — com o presidente francês, Emmanuel Macron, e o chanceler alemão, Friedrich Merz. Os líderes deveriam discutir o pedido da Ucrânia por mais sistemas de defesa aérea para impedir que mísseis balísticos russos bombardeiem cidades ucranianas. Vestindo uma camisa tradicional ucraniana bordada, Zelenskiy agradeceu a vários líderes estrangeiros por terem viajado até Kiev para demonstrar seu apoio. Ele prometeu encontrar uma solução para o que chamou de “terror balístico” do presidente russo, Vladimir Putin. “A Ucrânia deseja absolutamente a paz, mas não está pronta para simplesmente se render”, disse Zelenskiy em seu discurso em vídeo publicado no Telegram, que o mostrava em pé diante do mosteiro de São Miguel, com sua cúpula dourada. Zelenskiy afirmou que a exigência da Rússia — repetidamente rejeitada pela Ucrânia — de que Kiev ceda a parte restante da região de Donbas que ainda não está nas mãos da Rússia após 4 anos e meio de guerra não seria suficiente para deter a agressão russa. “A Ucrânia é diferente e não abre mão do que é seu”, disse ele. Centenas de milhares de pessoas foram mortas e vastas áreas do território ucraniano foram devastadas desde que a Rússia lançou sua invasão em grande escala em 24 de fevereiro de 2022. As negociações de paz lideradas pelos EUA para pôr um fim definitivo à guerra estagnaram, já que a Ucrânia recusou as exigências russas de ceder mais território, e os combates continuam ao longo de uma linha de frente de 1.200 km. Zelenskiy destacou as conquistas da indústria de defesa da Ucrânia durante a guerra, incluindo ataques com drones navais e ataques de médio e longo alcance no interior da Rússia, mas afirmou que ainda há muito a ser feito. Ele instou a fabricante de armas ucraniana Fire Point a acelerar a produção de seu míssil de cruzeiro Flamingo para levar a luta à Rússia neste inverno.

item.title: Ceasefire monitors deploy in eastern Congo under Qatari peace deal
item.description: A mission to observe implementation of a ceasefire between Congolese forces and Rwandan-backed rebels began on Monday in eastern Congo, the first field deployment under a monitoring mechanism established by a Qatari-mediated peace deal signed last year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A mission to observe implementation of a ceasefire between Congolese forces and Rwandan-backed rebels began on Monday in eastern Congo, the first field deployment under a monitoring mechanism established by a Qatari-mediated peace deal signed last year. The deployment of the mission is the latest sign of incremental progress under the Qatar-mediated talks, which began last year after AFC/M23 staged a lightning offensive in eastern Congo, [USN:L6N3XE158 TEXT:"seizing the region's two largest cities"]. The two sides signed a peace deal in November 2025 that established a framework for a comprehensive peace agreement and the implementation of ceasefire monitoring arrangements. The mission is taking place in the town of Minembwe, South Kivu province, which has seen a surge in fighting in recent weeks between AFC/M23 rebels and government forces, with each side accusing the other of ceasefire violations. AFC/M23 accused government forces on Monday of shelling a village near Minembwe, causing civilian casualties and displacing residents. A spokesperson for Congo's armed forces did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Congolese government and AFC/M23 representatives met in Switzerland last week and agreed on a new roadmap for negotiations, pointing to renewed momentum in the Doha peace process after months of stalled talks. The Doha process is running parallel to U.S.-mediated talks between Congo and Rwanda that Washington hopes will fuel Western investments in eastern Congo's minerals sector. Earlier this month, Congolese authorities [USN:L8N4440KH TEXT:"released 15 prisoners"] and handed them over to AFC/M23 rebels, in the first known transfer of prisoners under the deal. The rebels control large swathes of eastern Congo after staging their offensive last year.

item.title: India declare on 503-9 after Jurel hundred
item.description: India rode Dhruv Jurel's unbeaten hundred to reach 503-9 before declaring their first innings on day two of the second and final test against Sri Lanka in Colombo on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India rode Dhruv Jurel's unbeaten hundred to reach 503-9 before declaring their first innings on day two of the second and final test against Sri Lanka in Colombo on Monday. Jurel made 115 not out, his second test century, which included nine fours and two sixes. Jurel combined with Rishabh Pant in a 112-run stand for the seventh wicket to consolidate India's position. Pant, who had retired hurt with a forearm injury, returned to score a fluent 63. Asitha Fernando was the pick of the Sri Lankan bowlers with figures of 4-106. India are 1-0 ahead in the two-test series.

item.title: Red Sox heating up again entering series vs. Marlins
item.description: The Boston Red Sox, who were in last place before altering their season with a 27-3 run, will visit the Miami Marlins on Monday night for the opener of a three-game series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Boston Red Sox, who were in last place before altering their season with a 27-3 run, will visit the Miami Marlins on Monday night for the opener of a three-game series. Following their franchise-record 30-game run, the Red Sox staggered. They went 2-7 before getting back on track with a 5-1 homestand that concluded on Sunday with a 5-4 win over the San Francisco Giants. Perhaps the biggest example of Boston's turnaround is third baseman Caleb Durbin, who had a .530 OPS with just one home run through the end of May. Since then, he has an .859 OPS with 11 homers. But the three biggest offensive producers in the Red Sox lineup this year are first baseman Willson Contreras, right fielder Wilyer Abreu and center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela. Contreras, 34, still has elite bat speed and good plate discipline. He leads the Red Sox with a career-high 26 homers and also tops Boston regulars in OPS (.925) and RBIs (78). Abreu, who has an .800 OPS, is second on the team in doubles (27), homers (22) and RBIs (69). Rafaela, who has a .791 OPS, leads Boston in batting average (.289), doubles (32) and ranks fourth in homers (16) and third in RBIs (66). "If we stay with our approach, we feel like we're going to score more than three (runs per game)," Boston interim manager Chad Tracy said. On the mound on Monday, Boston will start left-hander Ranger Suarez (5-3, 3.41 ERA). In 22 career appearances (11 starts) against the Marlins, he is 7-2 with a 3.07 ERA, and he is 6-2 with a 2.47 ERA in 14 appearances at Miami's loanDepot Park. Meanwhile, the Marlins -- just like the Red Sox -- are coming off a three-game home sweep. Miami took down Washington for its ninth sweep of the season. Seven of those sweeps have come at home, where the Marlins are 41-25. Only three teams have more home wins than the Marlins -- the Tampa Bay Rays, Atlanta Braves and Milwaukee Brewers. Those three are all first-place teams while the Marlins are outside of a playoff spot in the National League. Joe Mack, Miami's impressive rookie catcher, said the Marlins have become a cohesive team at home. "We rally together," he said. "We put together good at-bats, and we have an amazing group of fans who support us every day. We love them." Since May 22, Miami is 26-10 at home, having won 10 of 12 series there. The Marlins will try to continue their home success on Monday night when they start their wins leader, right-hander Sandy Alcantara (13-8, 3.46 ERA). In three career starts against Boston, he is 1-1 with a 1.42 ERA. Another key for Miami is outfielder Heriberto Hernandez, especially against a left-handed pitcher such as Suarez. Hernandez leads the Marlins with a career-high 19 homers. Miami is 15-2 when Hernandez goes deep, and he leads the team with a .548 slugging percentage against lefties. The Marlins also have a lot of speed, ranking second in the majors with 132 steals. Esteury Ruiz leads the team with 29. --Field Level Media

item.title: IEA's Birol: not discussing a second release of strategic oil reserves
item.description: The International Energy Agency is not discussing a second release of strategic oil reserves at this time, IEA chief Fatih Birol told Reuters on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Nora Buli
item.content:encoded: The International Energy Agency is not discussing a second release of strategic oil reserves at this time, IEA chief Fatih Birol told Reuters on Monday. "Not for the time being," Birol said on the sidelines of an energy conference in Norway when asked whether the agency was discussing a second release of strategic reserves. The IEA is always following the markets "very, very closely", and 80% of strategic reserves remain after a 400 million-barrel release in March, Birol added. On gas, Birol expressed concerns Europe's [USN:L6N43Q0VZ TEXT:"current levels of gas reserves"], [USN:L8N44L0GU TEXT:"which are around 62%"] according to transparency platform AGSI. The European Union has a target of filling levels to 80% by December 1. "The stocks are lower than historical averages, and we are still hoping to get gas from the Middle East, and at the same time ... Europe has committed itself to nullify the Russian gas imports," he said. "If we have a harsh winter in Europe, we may have some challenges."

item.title: Vantagem numérica de Lula para Flávio diminui em 2° turno, ambos mantêm empate técnico, diz BTG/Nexus
item.description: A vantagem numérica do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) em um eventual segundo turno da eleição presidencial contra o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) diminuiu para um ponto percentual e ambos seguem em empate técnico, mostrou pesquisa BTG/Nexus divulgada nesta segunda-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A vantagem numérica do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) em um eventual segundo turno da eleição presidencial contra o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) diminuiu para um ponto percentual e ambos seguem em empate técnico, mostrou pesquisa BTG/Nexus divulgada nesta segunda-feira. O levantamento mostrou ainda manutenção da liderança de Lula no primeiro turno, com 41%, mesmo patamar da pesquisa de uma semana atrás, ao passo que Flávio soma agora 37%, ante 36% na semana passada. Nenhum outro candidato ultrapassa a marca de 5%. Em um eventual segundo turno entre Lula e Flávio, o presidente soma agora 46%, ante 47% uma semana atrás, ao passo que o senador pontua 45%, ante 44%. Desde a pesquisa BTG/Nexus de 29 de junho, ou seja, há sete semanas, Lula e Flávio vêm aparecendo em empate técnico dentro da margem de erro de 2 pontos percentuais, com vantagem numérica do petista. A pesquisa mostrou ainda que 49% rejeitam Lula, ante 48% na pesquisa anterior, e que 48% rejeitam Flávio, ante 50% uma semana atrás. De acordo com o levantamento do instituto Nexus, contratado pelo banco BTG Pactual, a avaliação negativa do governo Lula é de 43%, ante 42% uma semana atrás, ao passo que a positiva soma 35%, ante 34%, e a regular é de 22%, ante 23%. Ao mesmo tempo, 49% desaprovam o trabalho que vem sendo realizado por Lula, ante 48% na pesquisa anterior, e o percentual dos que aprovam é de 48%, ante 47%. O Nexus ouviu 2.006 pessoas entre os dias 21 e 23 de agosto. A margem de erro é de 2 pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos.

item.title: Grupos armados ilegales aumentan reclutamiento de niños, niñas y adolescentes en Colombia aprovechando redes sociales: HRW
item.description: El reclutamiento de niños, niñas y adolescentes por parte de grupos armados ilegales aumentó en los últimos años en Colombia, aprovechando la pobreza, la exclusión social, la falta de educación y el creciente uso de las redes sociales, reveló el lunes un informe de Human Rights Watch (HRW).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El reclutamiento de niños, niñas y adolescentes por parte de grupos armados ilegales aumentó en los últimos años en Colombia, aprovechando la pobreza, la exclusión social, la falta de educación y el creciente uso de las redes sociales, reveló el lunes un informe de Human Rights Watch (HRW). Un análisis de datos de la Defensoría del Pueblo realizado por la organización no gubernamental internacional dedicada a la investigación y defensa de los derechos humanos estableció que al menos 1.500 menores de edad fueron reclutados desde 2021, la mayoría por disidencias de la antigua guerrilla de las Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias de Colombia (FARC). "Los grupos armados en Colombia están reclutando a niños, niñas y adolescentes con impunidad, los sistemas de protección están fallando y las plataformas de redes sociales se han convertido en terreno fértil para el reclutamiento", dijo Juanita Goebertus, directora para las Américas de HRW, citada en un comunicado. Colombia enfrenta un conflicto armado interno de más de seis décadas que ha dejado cerca de 500.000 muertos y millones de desplazados. La mayoría de los casos documentados en el informe se registró en el departamento del Cauca, en el suroeste del país, y afectó a integrantes de pueblos indígenas entre los 10 y 14 años, lo que "podría considerarse un crimen de guerra según el derecho internacional", dijo HRW. El informe aseguró que los grupos armados ilegales han aprovechado las redes sociales para glorificar la vida en sus filas, publicar ofertas de trabajo que son, en esencia, artimañas destinadas al reclutamiento, y contactar a niños y niñas a través de foros de chat públicos y servicios de mensajería privada. La investigación denunció que las plataformas de redes sociales no han sido efectivas para detectar ni eliminar esos contenidos, y tampoco han prevenido adecuadamente su difusión. "En algunos casos, sus algoritmos parecían promover estas publicaciones, lo que muy probablemente amplió considerablemente el alcance de los grupos armados", sostuvo el informe. HRW manifestó que durante la investigación contactó a Meta, propietaria de Facebook, y a ByteDance, matriz de TikTok, para informarles sobre estos hallazgos. Ambas plataformas aseguraron que sus políticas prohíben la difusión de contenido que promueva, apoye o proclame organizaciones violentas, por lo que removieron algunos perfiles con contenido explícito de los grupos armados, incluyendo ofertas de reclutamiento. Los grupos armados acostumbran a trasladar a los niños y niñas a otras regiones para aislarlos, romper sus lazos familiares y comunitarios, y dificultar su escape, denunció HRW. "En algunos casos, estos reciben entrenamiento militar. En otros, son utilizados para recopilar información, servir como mensajeros, brindar atención médica, vigilar a rehenes, participar en actividades de tráfico de drogas o como guardaespaldas de los comandantes", aseguró el informe. "Las niñas están particularmente expuestas a violencia sexual", concluyó la investigación.

item.title: Oro toca pico de más de tres meses, mientras mercados esperan datos de inflación EEUU
item.description: El oro cotizaba el lunes en máximos de más de tres meses, ya que la debilidad del dólar potenciaba su atractivo, mientras los inversores esperan los datos de inflación en Estados Unidos y las declaraciones del presidente de la Reserva Federal, Kevin Warsh, de esta semana para obtener indicios sobre el camino de las tasas de interés.
item.dc:creator: Sukanya Mitra
item.content:encoded: El oro cotizaba el lunes en máximos de más de tres meses, ya que la debilidad del dólar potenciaba su atractivo, mientras los inversores esperan los datos de inflación en Estados Unidos y las declaraciones del presidente de la Reserva Federal, Kevin Warsh, de esta semana para obtener indicios sobre el camino de las tasas de interés. * A las 1004 GMT, el oro al contado ganaba un 1%, a 4.649,08 dólares por onza, alcanzando su nivel más alto desde el 15 de mayo, mientras que los futuros del oro en Estados Unidos avanzaban un 0,6%, a 4.706,2 dólares. * El oro mejoró más de un 5% la semana pasada, después de que el plan de apoyo mediante recompra del Departamento del Tesoro hiciera caer al dólar, abaratando el lingote —cotizado en el billete verde— para los inversores extranjeros. * "La consolidación de los precios del oro por encima de los 4.600 dólares y la posibilidad de nuevas subidas dependerán en gran medida de que el dólar siga bajo presión y de que el rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro se estabilice en los niveles actuales o siga bajando", afirmó Ricardo Evangelista, de ActivTrades. * El dólar operaba en la sesión cerca de sus mínimos de varios meses. * Los actores del mercado esperan ahora el índice de precios del gasto en consumo personal de julio, que se publicará el miércoles, y el discurso de Warsh en el Simposio de Jackson Hole el viernes para evaluar las perspectivas de las autoridades monetarias sobre las tasas. * Según la herramienta FedWatch de la CME, los operadores ven una probabilidad de alrededor del 36% de que se produzca un alza de tasas en septiembre, frente a un 64% de que la Fed las mantenga estables. * En otros metales preciosos, la plata al contado cotizaba estable en 68,93 dólares por onza; el platino subía un 0,1%, a 1.880,17 dólares; y el paladio caía un 0,4%, a 1.344,35 dólares.

item.title: India's TCS to buy Porsche's IT unit, bags 5-year deal worth $1.46 billion
item.description: Tata Consultancy Services will buy Porsche AG's automotive and consulting unit MHP, the IT major said on Monday, as part of a wider partnership under which Porsche has committed €1.25 billion ($1.46 billion) for the Indian firm and MHP.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS.NS) will buy Porsche AG's (P911_p.DE) automotive and consulting unit MHP, the IT major said on Monday, as part of a wider partnership under which Porsche has committed €1.25 billion ($1.46 billion) for the Indian firm and MHP. The deal comes at a time when AI has been [USN:L1N40R0IW TEXT:"disrupting"] traditional outsourcing models in India's $315 billion IT industry with clients pausing tech spends. MHP is an automotive and industrial consulting firm that specializes in business consulting and software-defined mobility. The deal, for an enterprise value of €320 million, is expected to close in the next 3-4 months, TCS said. The wider five-year pact is tied to deploying AI across Porsche's engineering, manufacturing, operations and customer experience verticals, as well as developing automotive technology and software-defined mobility platforms, TCS said. Porsche is part of the Volkswagen group, which is under pressure to cut costs and trim back its sprawling portfolio as it faces pressure from Chinese competitors, tariffs and EV costs. The firm sold stakes in sports car makers Bugatti and Rimac earlier this year and scrapped three subsidiaries including its battery unit Cellforce and e-bike business, costing over 500 jobs. "The deal will be adding to TCS revenue. It is similar to Harman DTS, Olam acquisitions done by Wipro (WIPR.NS) where companies would land and expand. It will have a neutral impact on the stock and overall capability of the company," said Piyush Pandey, an IT analyst at brokerage Centrum Broking. ($1 = 0.8573 euros)

item.title: Grid bottlenecks push businesses toward larger onsite power systems, Capstone says
item.description: Rising demand for onsite power among businesses struggling to secure capacity from strained American utilities is propelling orders for larger generation blocks at Capstone Energy+ , CEO Vince Canino said in an interview with Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Arunima Kumar
item.content:encoded: Rising demand for onsite power among businesses struggling to secure capacity from strained American utilities is propelling orders for larger generation blocks at Capstone Energy+ (CEPL.O) , CEO Vince Canino said in an interview with Reuters. As grid constraints grow, businesses are increasingly viewing onsite generation as a way to secure power for expansion rather than simply a means of reducing energy costs. Capstone, which provides microturbine and behind-the-meter power systems for commercial and industrial customers, is seeing demand from sectors including healthcare and is pursuing data-center projects. "Today's discussions are truly about energy certainty," Canino said. Capstone is now seeing customers buy larger blocks of power, including 3, 4 and 6-megawatt systems, compared with smaller projects that were more typical in the past, Canino said. A 1-megawatt power system can typically supply electricity to roughly 750-1,000 homes at a given time, depending on average household demand and location. Customers are also moving faster to secure onsite power as they face delays in obtaining utility capacity. "I think today a lot of those cycles are shrinking because it's no longer about, well, is this a really good investment and what's the return? It's more about I need power and I've got to make sure I have it on demand," Canino said. Capstone recently installed a 2 MW combined heat and power system at Scripps Mercy Hospital in San Diego, providing electricity and backup power during outages. The company has deployed its technology at small enterprise data centers but has yet to deploy it at a large-scale data center, Canino said.

item.title: Oil’s elevated price could yet become a floor
item.description: Crude is trading at $92 a barrel, but de-escalation, reserve releases and softer demand could send it lower. Still, buffers are thinning just as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent threatens 'the greatest financial offensive ever'. If Hormuz stays impaired, prices will stay high.
item.dc:creator: Yawen Chen
item.content:encoded: Oil traders are running out of reasons to relax. Over the past three months, Brent crude has traded well below the $120-a-barrel peaks seen in March and April, despite severe disruption around the Strait of Hormuz. That relative calm rested on three fragile supports: hopes that Washington and Tehran would eventually reach an agreement, the release of emergency government reserves, and weaker demand, especially from China. The first of those looks shakiest. The 60-day window for a U.S.-Iran agreement expired last Monday without a deal, and U.S. President Donald Trump says no talks are planned. Meanwhile, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is promising a sweeping [USN:S8N40O00O TEXT:"financial offensive"] that could extend pressure to countries trading with Tehran. That may squeeze Iran economically but is unlikely to lead to a full-blown reopening of Hormuz. If anything, it could provoke further Iranian retaliation. Meanwhile, the world has already blown through much of the oil reserves mobilised as insurance against the war. International Energy Agency (IEA) members agreed in March to release 400 million barrels of emergency stocks. By July, about 290 million barrels had been released - equivalent to roughly five weeks of the 8 million barrels a day of Middle Eastern supply that analysts estimate is offline. China also helped absorb the shock by cutting crude imports sharply, while Gulf producers pushed more oil through alternative routes including Saudi Arabia’s pipeline to Yanbu on the Red Sea and the United Arab Emirates’s pipeline to Fujairah outside Hormuz. Now inventories are under more strain. Analysts at Vortexa reckon oil being carried at sea fell by 211 million barrels in the 40 days since mid-July, while oil stored in tanks on land dropped by another 94 million barrels. If the fall at sea merely reflected tankers arriving and unloading, onshore stocks should have risen. Instead, they fell too, which suggests the market is burning through both buffers at once. Together, that means roughly 300 million fewer barrels were readily available to meet demand. Onshore stocks are now about 93 million barrels below their seasonal average, having been 127 million above it in late March. The remaining supply fixes are similarly fragile. Hormuz traffic was about 90% below late-February levels in the week to August 16, according to Lloyd’s List, while Houthi threats are making Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea bypass less dependable. Refiners have little incentive to ease the pressure either: shortages of diesel and other fuels have kept [USN:L6N44A13E TEXT:"processing margins unusually high"]. The oil bears can still argue their case. China has already shown it can [USN:L6N43Q0R7 TEXT:"consume and process less oil"], while governments retain substantial emergency reserves. Trump may also seek a compromise if expensive fuel becomes politically intolerable. Yet none of those fixes resolves a prolonged Hormuz disruption. If inventories continue to fall, escalation by the U.S. or Iran could send crude above $100. Even without one, today’s $92 may start to look like the floor. Follow Yawen Chen on Bluesky and LinkedIn . The U.S. threatened Iran with what it called "the greatest financial offensive ever marshalled" as it prepared to roll out economic sanctions on August 24 that target Iran's trade partners. "At dawn begins an economic D-Day — the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary," U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wrote in an opinion piece published in the Financial Times on August 23. Brent crude futures fell $1.49, or 1.6%, to $92.90 by 0649 GMT on August 24, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude was at $85.32 a barrel, down $1.74, or 2%. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: AfD turns 'Vespa of East Germany' into election campaign vehicle
item.description: The sound of thousands of engines filled the festival grounds of the medieval German village of Quedlinburg on Sunday as Ulrich Siegmund, the far-right AfD's charismatic candidate in a key vote next month, led out a motorcade atop a blue moped.
item.dc:creator: Miranda Murray
item.content:encoded: The sound of thousands of engines filled the festival grounds of the medieval German village of Quedlinburg on Sunday as Ulrich Siegmund, the far-right AfD's charismatic candidate in a key vote next month, led out a motorcade atop a blue moped. Nearly 5,000 people turned out for the Alternative for Germany (AfD) campaign event-cum-motorcycle show [USN:L1N44K02T TEXT:"ahead of elections"] in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt on September 6, in which it could become the first far-right party to [USN:L1N43O0DH TEXT:"take power"] at a state level since the Nazi era. The AfD has seized onto "the Vespa of East Germany," the beloved Simson brand, to appeal to the strong sense of [USN:L8N41S22I TEXT:"East German identity"] that lingers 35 years after reunification, even as a significant number of young people, including Siegmund, never experienced a divided Germany themselves. SIMSON BRINGS BACK POSITIVE MEMORIES "My parents instilled in me an understanding of everything that happened back then. Not everything was wonderful," the 35-year-old Siegmund told the crowd on Sunday. "But this Simson culture represents individual freedom of movement. It stands for a time when we in this country stuck together," he said. The AfD's manifesto "Vision 2026" argues that eastern Germany should be seen as a model for the rest of the country rather than a disadvantaged region. Based on the 2025 federal election, their strategy is working. Among Saxony-Anhalt voters aged roughly 18-34, AfD support rose to 40% from about 25% in the previous election in 2021. Julian, who declined to give his last name, said it was great the AfD was organising meet-ups for fans. "If someone else had done it, we obviously wouldn't have taken part," said the 24-year-old from the neighbouring eastern German state of Thuringia who, along with his brother, attended Sunday's event with his green Simson motorcycle. BRAND WITH HISTORY The Simson company began as a weapons manufacturer run by two Jewish brothers in the mid-19th century whose family was forced to flee as the Nazis rose to power. After World War Two and the separation of Germany, the company focused on motorcycles and mopeds, with their distinctive Schwalbe, known as the "Vespa of East Germany," and sporty S50 becoming particularly popular models with young people by letting them bypass the often years-long waiting period for cars. The Simson family, who now live in the United States, have publicly criticised the AfD's use of their namesake. "The threats against immigrants, people of other skin colours and sexual minorities are something we want no part of," said descendent and family spokesperson Dennis Baum at an anti-AfD rally in Germany last month. The AfD has rejected allegations of racism, saying it just wants stricter controls over immigration. The Center for Intercultural Understanding Dresden (ZVID) is running an online petition with nearly 24,000 signatories calling on the current trademark holder to protect the brand's reputation by sending a cease-and-desist letter to the AfD. Roughly 100 counter-demonstrators at Sunday's event were cordoned off by police in a lot whose view of the grounds was obscured by trees and throngs of supporters. ROOTS OF EAST GERMAN IDENTITY East German identity emerged mainly after reunification, shaped by the experience of adapting to West German political, economic and cultural structures and by feelings of disadvantage, according to sociologist Daniel Kubiak from the Humboldt University of Berlin. This shared feeling of structural disadvantage and unequal opportunities, which young people learned through their parents' experiences, has often been neglected by mainstream politics, creating space for the AfD to appeal to eastern voters through identity politics, he added. While eastern Germany has largely caught up in terms of living standards, many young people still report concerns about financial security: A 2024 government-commissioned survey found 67% of respondents from the east considered it most important, versus 62% of their western peers. However, Kubiak described the AfD's version of East German identity as vague and inconsistent, arguing the party mainly uses feelings of devaluation and marginalisation to mobilise support rather than offering a coherent East German identity. "The AfD's identity narrative can always adapt very well to where they are," he said.

item.title: Sable Offshore fined $1.45 million, allowed to continue pipeline operations
item.description: Sable Offshore said on Monday a U.S. judge fined the oil and gas producer $1.45 million for violating a pipeline consent decree, but declined California's request to halt operations of its Santa Ynez Pipeline System.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Sable Offshore (SOC.N) said on Monday a U.S. judge fined the oil and gas producer $1.45 million for violating a pipeline consent decree, but declined California's request to halt operations of its Santa Ynez Pipeline System. The rulings allow Sable to continue working to restart and expand its Santa Ynez project, which it has been trying to revive since a 2015 pipeline spill. Here are more details: The court found Sable violated the 2020 consent decree by restarting pipeline operations without authorization from California's state fire marshal. The judge ruled the company was no longer in violation after the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration approved its restart plan. It [USN:L2N3VW037 TEXT:"restarted"] production from one of the project's offshore platforms last year, nearly a decade after operations were halted following a 2015 oil spill under former owner ExxonMobil (XOM.N) . In a separate case, the judge denied California's bid to block a federal Defense Production Act order supporting Sable's pipeline operations and ruled that the state's Department of Parks and Recreation could not take legal action to prevent Sable from complying. California has appealed the decision denying its request for a preliminary injunction, while another defendant appealed a related declaratory judgment.

item.title: U.S. court orders Guardant to pay $245 million in DNA sequencing patent dispute
item.description: A U.S. court has ordered Guardant Health to pay more than $245.2 million to TwinStrand Biosciences and the University of Washington after finding that the company infringed patents covering DNA sequencing technology, TwinStrand said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A U.S. court has ordered Guardant Health to pay more than $245.2 million to TwinStrand Biosciences and the University of Washington after finding that the company infringed patents covering DNA sequencing technology, TwinStrand said on Monday. Here are the details: The U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware entered final judgment on August 21, upholding a [USN:L1N3CG1HD TEXT:"2023 jury verdict"] that found Guardant had willfully infringed two patents related to TwinStrand's DNA sequencing technology. The court ordered Guardant to pay a 6% royalty on U.S. sales of 11 products and services found to infringe the patents until they expire in March 2033. The judgment includes $83.4 million in original damages, $19.5 million in supplemental damages, $119.4 million in accrued royalties, and $22.9 million in pre- and post-judgment interest. TwinStrand said the products and services covered by the ruling accounted for about 90% of Guardant's revenue during the infringement period. The products covered by the ruling include Guardant360 CDx, Guardant Reveal, the Shield cancer test and several other cancer testing and genomics services sold by Guardant. Guardant had sought to overturn the verdict or obtain a new trial, but the court rejected those efforts, TwinStrand said. The judgment also upheld the validity of the patent claims at issue, TwinStrand said. TwinStrand's Duplex Sequencing technology is designed to detect rare genetic mutations with greater accuracy than conventional DNA sequencing methods. TwinStrand said its technology, developed at the University of Washington, is used in cancer research, diagnostics and drug development.

item.title: FDA places clinical hold on Regenxbio's gene therapy for Hunter Syndrome
item.description: Regenxbio said on Monday the U.S. FDA has placed its experimental gene therapy for a rare inherited disorder on clinical hold after spinal scans found abnormalities in five study participants, sending its shares down more than 24% in premarket trading.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Regenxbio (RGNX.O) said on Monday the U.S. FDA has placed its experimental gene therapy for a rare inherited disorder on clinical hold after spinal scans found abnormalities in five study participants, sending its shares down more than 24% in premarket trading. The therapy, RGX-121, was being developed as a one-time treatment for Hunter Syndrome, also known as MPS II, which can cause progressive damage to the brain and other organs and tissues. The spinal scans identified a small lump or fluid-filled mass in the patients who received the treatment, RGX-121, about three to six years ago, the biotech said. The setback adds to Regenxbio's regulatory troubles after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration [USN:L4N3Z51ZK TEXT:"declined to approve"] RGX-121 earlier this year over concerns about the trial design and supporting evidence. RGX-121 was also subject to the health regulator's previous [USN:L4N3YT1EW TEXT:"clinical hold"] on the company's two gene therapy programs. The therapy uses a harmless virus known as AAV9 vector to deliver the gene needed to produce the missing enzyme in patients with Hunter syndrome. Current treatment options include Takeda Pharmaceutical's (4502.T) Elaprase, a weekly infusion that treats the physical effects of Hunter syndrome, and Denali Therapeutics' (DNLI.O) Avlayah, [USN:L4N40D1JV TEXT:"approved in March"], to treat neurological symptoms in certain children. Regenxbio said the five patients remained asymptomatic and were clinically stable or showed improvements in cognitive and behavioral assessments. Trial investigators deemed the findings to be non-serious and radiologists believed they were likely benign. The company said it does not expect to resubmit its application for the treatment's approval in the near term. It, along with partner NS Pharma, will review additional imaging and longer-term follow-up data and await the FDA's full clinical hold letter before deciding the next steps for RGX-121.

item.title: Envelhecimento da população da Alemanha leva gastos sociais a máxima recorde, afirma Ifo
item.description: Os gastos combinados relacionados à população mais velha e às doenças representaram cerca de 70% do total dos gastos sociais da Alemanha no ano passado, levando o orçamento social a uma nova máxima recorde, de acordo com uma análise do Instituto Ifo publicada nesta segunda-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os gastos combinados relacionados à população mais velha e às doenças representaram cerca de 70% do total dos gastos sociais da Alemanha no ano passado, levando o orçamento social a uma nova máxima recorde, de acordo com uma análise do Instituto Ifo publicada nesta segunda-feira. A análise constatou que os gastos relacionados à população mais velha e às doenças foram responsáveis por mais de 80% do aumento real nos gastos desde 1992. O principal fator estrutural por trás dessa tendência é a mudança demográfica. "O orçamento social está crescendo mais rapidamente do que o PIB, e é por isso que a economia fraca também está contribuindo para o aumento da fatia do orçamento social”, afirmou a pesquisadora do Ifo Emilie Hoeslinger. De acordo com a análise, os gastos sociais aumentaram 11,5%, ou 104 bilhões de euros, entre 2019 e 2025, ajustados pelos efeitos da inflação. Durante esse período, a fatia do orçamento social atingiu um novo recorde, passando de 29,6% para 32%. Os principais fatores são os gastos adicionais com doenças e cuidados para a população idosa segurada, bem como os pagamentos federais mais elevados de aposentadorias. (Reportagem de Maria Martinez)

item.title: Mediador Paquistão realizará negociações no Irã enquanto EUA preparam “Dia D econômico”
item.description: O chefe do Exército do Paquistão estava em Teerã nesta segunda-feira em uma missão de mediação, enquanto os Estados Unidos se preparavam para lançar “a maior ofensiva financeira de todos os tempos” contra os parceiros comerciais do Irã.
item.dc:creator: Menna Alaa El-Din, Asif Shahzad, Ariba Shahid
item.content:encoded: O chefe do Exército do Paquistão estava em Teerã nesta segunda-feira em uma missão de mediação, enquanto os Estados Unidos se preparavam para lançar “a maior ofensiva financeira de todos os tempos” contra os parceiros comerciais do Irã. O Irã rejeitou a ameaça dos EUA, prometendo interromper todas as exportações de petróleo do Golfo “se a guerra econômica continuar”. O país emitiu uma nova advertência aos navios para que não atravessassem o Estreito de Ormuz sem sua permissão, listando 45 embarcações que, segundo ele, teriam violado suas regras e ameaçando retaliar qualquer transferência de navio para navio envolvendo essas embarcações. O secretário do Tesouro dos EUA, Scott Bessent, prometeu revelar medidas severas contra o Irã — que vem sofrendo sanções econômicas quase contínuas desde a Revolução Islâmica de 1979 — durante uma coletiva de imprensa marcada para 14h (horário de Brasília) desta segunda-feira. “Ao amanhecer, começa um ‘Dia D’ econômico — a maior ofensiva financeira já mobilizada contra um adversário”, escreveu Bessent em um artigo de opinião publicado no Financial Times no domingo. O chefe do Exército do Paquistão, Asim Munir, que construiu um relacionamento pessoal com o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, chegou ao Irã na segunda-feira para conversações, informou a mídia iraniana. O Paquistão disse que a visita faz parte de seus esforços “para promover a paz e a estabilidade regionais”, e uma fonte paquistanesa declarou que Munir deveria se reunir com pessoas próximas ao líder supremo do Irã. Duas fontes paquistanesas afirmaram que Trump ligou para Munir na semana passada, e uma outra disse que o principal pedido era fazer com que o Irã voltasse às negociações. A Casa Branca não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário. EUA e Irã não realizam ataques aéreos contra as forças armadas um do outro há semanas, mas suas últimas negociações oficiais presenciais para pôr fim ao conflito, que já dura seis meses, ocorreram em junho, e os ataques a embarcações no Estreito de Ormuz continuaram. Um projétil atingiu um petroleiro a oeste da cidade portuária saudita de Yanbu, no Mar Vermelho, na segunda-feira, causando um incêndio no convés principal, segundo informaram monitores de tráfego marítimo da Maritime Trade Operations, do Reino Unido. Eles não revelaram quem teria lançado o projétil. Os aliados houthis do Irã afirmaram no mês passado que bloqueariam as exportações de petróleo sauditas desviadas para o Mar Vermelho a fim de evitar o Estreito de Ormuz. Milhares de pessoas morreram, a maioria delas no Irã e no Líbano, desde que EUA e Israel iniciaram os ataques em 28 de fevereiro, prejudicando grande parte da capacidade militar convencional do Irã e causando danos econômicos, além de terem matado o então líder supremo do Irã, aiatolá Ali Khamenei. No entanto, o Irã preservou capacidade suficiente de mísseis e drones para atacar seus vizinhos do Golfo e praticamente paralisar a navegação no Estreito de Ormuz, elevando os preços mundiais dos combustíveis. O estado exato do programa nuclear iraniano, que os norte-americanos e israelenses pretendem eliminar, permanece desconhecido. Os preços do petróleo recuaram na segunda-feira, após duas semanas de alta, à medida que os investidores realizaram lucros antes do anúncio esperado pelos EUA. Sem detalhar medidas específicas, Bessent sinalizou que os EUA teriam como alvo “nações temerosas” que praticam a “apaziguamento” ao se envolverem com a economia e o sistema financeiro do Irã. “Fariam bem em considerar as consequências de manter essa postura”, escreveu ele no Financial Times. O Irã vem se preparando para as sanções há dias, emitindo uma série de declarações que sugerem uma resposta militar de grande porte. Mohsen Rezaei, secretário do Conselho Supremo de Segurança Nacional do Irã, sugeriu, no domingo, uma retaliação econômica. “Se a guerra econômica continuar, nem uma única gota de petróleo será exportada, nem pelo Estreito de Ormuz nem de qualquer outro lugar do Golfo Pérsico”, escreveu Rezaei em uma postagem nas redes sociais. “O Irã considerará a participação ou o apoio de qualquer país à guerra econômica dos Estados Unidos contra o povo iraniano como um ato de guerra.”

item.title: Rays' Drew Rasmussen eager to continue win streak in opener vs. Tigers
item.description: The Tampa Bay Rays snapped a three-game losing streak on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Tampa Bay Rays snapped a three-game losing streak on Sunday. The American League East-leading Rays will try to build off that victory on Monday night in the opener of a three-game road series against the struggling Detroit Tigers. Tampa Bay won 3-1 on Sunday to salvage the finale of a three-game series in Baltimore. Even with that victory, the Rays have dropped seven of their last 10 games but still hold a three-game advantage over the second-place New York Yankees in the division. "I don't think we're firing on all cylinders right now, but you'll take it however you can get it," Tampa Bay manager Kevin Cash said. The Rays scored all of their runs Sunday in the sixth inning. Nick Martinez and three relievers combined to hold the Orioles to two hits. "At this time of year, and looking at our schedule, we're facing a lot of guys whose backs are up against the wall, right?" Martinez told MLB.com. "They have to win every game for them to make it to the playoffs, so we've just got to match the energy, bring the energy and keep playing to win ballgames. "Keep doing what the game's asking us to do and playing our style, and things will turn around. Obviously you want to be winning every game you can, but the most important games are still in front of us." Tampa Bay right-hander Drew Rasmussen (13-5, 3.01 ERA) will start the series opener against Detroit. Rasmussen has recorded the victory in each of his last six starts, though the offense bailed him out in his last outing against Toronto on Wednesday. He gave up five runs in five innings, but the Rays won 7-6. The two-time All-Star hasn't faced the Tigers this season. In four career outings (two starts) against them, he's 1-0 with a 1.69 ERA. He'll oppose left-hander Framber Valdez (8-8, 4.35 ERA), who also picked up the victory in his last outing despite a tough start. He gave up five runs (four earned) in 5 2/3 innings against Pittsburgh in an 8-5 Detroit win on Monday. That was the lone win in Detroit's last nine games. The Tigers were swept by last-place Kansas City over the weekend, including an 11-7 loss on Sunday, to complete a 1-5 road trip. They were swept in a three-game series by the first-place Chicago White Sox prior to the trip. "We've got to pick ourselves up," Tigers manager A.J. Hinch said. "This was a miserable road trip, and the results make that pretty obvious. We show up every day ready to play. The environment is good. The want-to is there. We haven't executed perfectly, but we don't have to be perfect to win games. But at the end of the day, you either take a step forward or a step backward. We took a couple of steps backward on this trip, and we are wearing it." The Tigers' current homestand will include a three-game set against the Los Angeles Dodgers. "I understand the tough path we've created for ourselves," Hinch said of the Tigers, who are 3 1/2 games out of the AL's final wild-card spot. "But I don't care how bleak it looks. We need to show up ready to play against the Rays because they're pretty good." Valdez is 2-1 with a 3.60 ERA in three career appearances (all starts) against Tampa Bay. --Field Level Media

item.title: French far-left leader Melenchon seen reaching presidential runoff, poll shows
item.description: French far-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon is seen as the most likely rival to far-right candidate Marine Le Pen in next year's presidential run-off, a Monday poll showed, underlining a deeply polarised electorate as Emmanuel Macron's presidency draws to a close.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: French far-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon is seen as the most likely rival to far-right candidate Marine Le Pen in next year's presidential run-off, a Monday poll showed, underlining a deeply polarised electorate as Emmanuel Macron's presidency draws to a close. Melenchon, the candidate of the far-left France Unbowed (LFI) party, is seen reaching a run-off in at least three of the five scenarios polled, while he tied for second place in a fourth scenario. Le Pen is seen beating him easily in a run-off. The poll makes sobering reading for France's centrist candidates who are struggling to reach an electorate that is increasingly polarised. As Macron's second and final term comes to an end, the unpopular president leaves behind a hollowed-out political centre and weak economy, opening space for hardline parties, such as LFI and Le Pen's National Rally. "The risk of Mrs Le Pen and Mr Melenchon facing each other in the second round is real and serious," centrist candidate Edouard Philippe told reporters on Monday. Melenchon was seen winning around 16% to 17% in the first round, while Le Pen would get 35% to 38% of votes. Le Pen would win 64% of the votes against Melenchon in the run-off. Melenchon has already run three times for president in 2012, 2017 and 2022 but has never managed to reach the second round.

item.title: Equinor, Aker BP and Vaar target major Norway oil, gas discoveries
item.description: Equinor , Aker BP and Vaar Energi are teaming up to drill wells in less explored areas of Norway's continental shelf, aiming to make major new oil and gas discoveries after years of smaller finds, they said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Nerijus Adomaitis
item.content:encoded: Equinor (EQNR.OL) , Aker BP (AKRBP.OL) and Vaar Energi (VAR.OL) are teaming up to drill wells in less explored areas of Norway's continental shelf, aiming to make major new oil and gas discoveries after years of smaller finds, they said on Monday. Drilling in areas that have seen little or no prior exploration activity is more expensive than in mature regions and is associated with greater risk of drilling dry holes, but could also yield bigger finds. "By joining forces we are improving the exploration portfolio and we are also reducing the risk," Kjetil Hove, Equinor's head of Norwegian operations, told a joint press conference. The three companies have agreed to combine expertise, data, technology and exploration capacity to pursue selected high impact exploration opportunities, they said. Much of Norway's drilling in recent years concentrated on finding reserves around existing oil and gas fields, yielding a number of smaller discoveries that were quickly brought into production. "Near-field exploration remains crucial, but we also need to pursue bigger opportunities to sustain activity and value creation beyond 2035," Hove said. Norway's output is set to sharply decline during the next decade unless significant new finds are made, government forecasts show. Over the next four to five years, the three companies plan to mature and test a portfolio of approximately 20 to 25 exploration opportunities, with an ambition to drill around five high-impact wells annually. Starting in 2028, the combined annual drilling cost is estimated at around $750 million, divided equally between the three, they said. Most of the initial drilling would take place at Haltenbanken in the Norwegian Sea, but could extend to all parts of Norway's continental shelf, Hove told Reuters. Norway, Europe's largest oil and gas producer, [USN:L8N44I0B4 TEXT:"encourages energy firms to drill"] for more reserves, hoping to extend the life of its petroleum industry for decades to come despite concerns from environmental groups over the [USN:L6N44L0CB TEXT:"climate impact"].

item.title: Minério de ferro sobe com novos sinais de estímulos da China
item.description: Os contratos futuros do minério de ferro subiram nesta segunda-feira, impulsionados por novos sinais de estímulo da China e pelas expectativas de uma demanda mais forte antes do pico da temporada de construção, em setembro.
item.dc:creator: Emily Yong
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros do minério de ferro subiram nesta segunda-feira, impulsionados por novos sinais de estímulo da China e pelas expectativas de uma demanda mais forte antes do pico da temporada de construção, em setembro. O contrato de minério de ferro para janeiro mais negociado na Bolsa de Mercadorias de Dalian (DCE) da China fechou o pregão do dia com alta de 1,27%, a 716 iuanes (US$106,52) por tonelada. A referência de minério de ferro para setembro na Bolsa de Cingapura subia 1,72%, para US$97,35 por tonelada. A China lançará um novo pacote de medidas para expandir a demanda interna e impulsionar o crescimento econômico, afirmou o vice-ministro das Finanças, Liao Min, em uma coletiva de imprensa na sexta-feira, segundo a mídia estatal. Separadamente, a Comissão Nacional de Desenvolvimento e Reforma da China realizou reuniões consecutivas na semana passada, instando os governos locais a acelerarem a construção de grandes projetos, segundo reportagens da mídia local. A taxa de operação dos altos-fornos em 247 siderúrgicas subiu para 82,8% na semana passada, um aumento de 0,16 ponto percentual em relação à semana anterior, segundo dados da consultoria Mysteel. Espera-se que o foco do mercado mude gradualmente no final de agosto, passando das condições fracas do período de baixa sazonal para as expectativas de melhora na demanda durante a alta temporada, afirmou Yang Huidan, analista da corretora chinesa Guoyuan Futures, em nota. A reposição antecipada de estoques antes da alta temporada de setembro deverá ser uma força motriz de uma recuperação gradual dos preços do aço, disse Yang. (Reportagem de Emily Ou Yong)

item.title: TotalEnergies profitably moving heavily discounted oil through Strait of Hormuz, says CEO
item.description: French oil major TotalEnergies is profitably moving oil through the Strait of Hormuz, with higher transport costs more than offset by steep discounts from crude producers, its CEO said at a Norwegian energy conference on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Nora Buli, Nerijus Adomaitis
item.content:encoded: French oil major TotalEnergies (TTEF.PA) is profitably moving oil through the Strait of Hormuz, with higher transport costs more than offset by steep discounts from crude producers, its CEO said at a Norwegian energy conference on Monday. "We are today probably the largest trader of oil from Iraq or from Qatar ... and I can tell you that today crude oil is moving through the Strait of Hormuz very quietly, not publicly," said CEO Patrick Pouyanne. The Strait of Hormuz, previously a key transit route for a fifth of global oil and LNG supplies, has been paralysed during the U.S. and Israeli war with Iran owing to threats of bombing and mines. Pouyanne and others have called for investment in [USN:L6N42V108 TEXT:"alternative routes"] for oil to leave the Middle East, but the TotalEnergies boss said on Monday that the route remains profitable for those who can find ship owners willing to cross the strait. MIDDLE EAST OIL DISCOUNTED TO $30 BELOW BRENT "Crude oil is sold to you at $50, $60 per barrel, not the Brent price, because the producers are desperate to push their oil into the market," Pouyanne said. Brent crude futures were above $90 a barrel on Monday. "It costs more or less $20 million to move a VLCC (very large crude carrier) through Hormuz and come back ... divided by 2 million barrels of oil, that's an extra $10 a barrel," the CEO added. The same was not true for refined oil products because of smaller capacity of those ships, resulting in an unsustainable $50 a barrel surcharge for transport. "That's why you don't have a single tanker of products moving out of Hormuz ... So you have today a lack of oil products. That's why you have a bearish crude oil market and a very bullish products market, which is very strange," Pouyanne said. ALTERNATIVE EXPORT ROUTES STILL NEEDED TotalEnergies still plans to invest in alternative routes. "We will become partners of the pipeline moving from Baghdad to Syria, but I will also invest in Abu Dhabi, in doubling the Fujairah pipeline," Pouyanne said. The existing Abu Dhabi Crude Oil Pipeline, also known as the Habshan-Fujairah pipeline, can carry up to 1.8 million barrels per day and has proved crucial as the United Arab Emirates seeks to maximise exports from the Gulf of Oman coast, just outside Hormuz. The UAE hopes to [USN:L6N41S0IK TEXT:"double"] that export capacity by next year.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: I futures sull’S&P 500 e sul Nasdaq sono in calo mentre gli investitori si preparano ad affrontare una importante settimana segnata dalla prospettiva di nuove sanzioni Usa contro l’Iran, dal discorso del presidente della Fed Kevin Warsh a Jackson Hole e dai risultati di Nvidia, società di riferimento per l'IA. ** Gli Stati Uniti sono pronti a introdurre sanzioni economiche contro i partner commerciali dell’Iran, in quella che ha definito "la più grande offensiva finanziaria di sempre" e il segretario al Tesoro Scott Bessent terrà una conferenza stampa in serata. ** I prezzi del greggio scendono di oltre 1 dollaro il barile, con gli investitori impegnati nelle prese di profitto dopo i recenti rialzi in vista dell’annuncio. ** I timori per l’aumento dei prezzi dell’energia e il debito pubblico in forte crescita hanno spinto al rialzo i rendimenti dei titoli del Tesoro Usa la scorsa settimana, con il rendimento del 30 anni che ha toccato i massimi degli ultimi 19 anni, prima che il Tesoro annunciasse misure di sostegno. ** L'impennata dei rendimenti ha messo sotto pressione i titoli tech, orientati alla crescita, lasciando il settore Information Technology dell'S&P 500 (.SPLRCT) in calo di oltre il 3% sull'intera settimana. ** La pressione rimane elevata anche all'inizio di questa settimana, mentre l'attenzione degli investitori si sposta ai risultati trimestrali di Nvidia, la società con la maggiore capitalizzazione di mercato al mondo, attesi per mercoledì. Qualsiasi segnale di rallentamento della crescita potrebbe riaccendere i timori sulle valutazioni troppo elevate e sulla sostenibilità del rally guidato dall'intelligenza artificiale. ** "Anche risultati eccezionali potrebbero non garantire una reazione positiva, visto il recente deterioramento del sentiment nei confronti dei colossi dell’IA", ha affermato Ipek Ozkardeskaya, analista senior presso Swissquote Bank. ** "Con gli ottimi utili del secondo trimestre già scontati nei prezzi, i timori relativi ai finanziamenti per l’intelligenza artificiale e le notizie di carattere politico e geopolitico stanno gradualmente prendendo il sopravvento sull’andamento del mercato", ha aggiunto. ** Sabato Bloomberg News ha scritto che ad alcuni dei maggiori clienti di Nvidia è stato comunicato che i prezzi dei server dotati dei suoi chip per l’IA aumenteranno, in molti casi, di oltre il 15%. ** Oggi l’andamento delle megacap è misto: APPLE (AAPL.O) , NVIDIA (NVDA.O) e AMAZON.COM (AMZN.O) registrano un rialzo rispettivamente dello 0,4%, dello 0,1% e dello 0,02% nel premarket, mentre ALPHABET (GOOGL.O) perde lo 0,3%. ** Anche la maggior parte dei produttori di chip è in calo. Tra le società di archiviazione dati SANDISK (SNDK.O) perde il 5% e SEAGATE (STX.O) cede il 3,3%. ** Il titolo di ALIBABA (9988.HK) , quotato negli Stati Uniti perde il 2,2% dopo che il gigante cinese dell’e-commerce ha lanciato una vendita di azioni da 10,2 miliardi di dollari con uno sconto consistente per finanziare le proprie ambizioni nel campo dell’IA. ** Alle 12.30 italiane i futures E-mini sul Dow sono in calo dello 0,04%, i futures E-mini sull'S&P 500 perdono lo 0,15% e i futures E-mini sul Nasdaq 100 cedono lo 0,53%. ** Nel frattempo, il discorso di Warsh al simposio annuale della Fed a Jackson Hole, in Wyoming, sarà seguito con grande attenzione questa settimana alla ricerca di indicazioni su come la banca centrale intenda gestire la politica monetaria in un contesto di aumento dei prezzi del greggio e dei rendimenti dei titoli di Stato. ** "Non sappiamo più chi controllerà in definitiva la parte lunga della curva dei rendimenti Usa: il Tesoro, la Fed o il mercato obbligazionario stesso ... Dopo la reazione della scorsa settimana all’annuncio del Tesoro, è ancora il mercato ad avere l’ultima parola", ha affermato Ozkardeskaya. ** "L’incontro di Jackson Hole farà un po’ di chiarezza su come la Fed si inserirà in questo contesto", ha aggiunto. ** Secondo i dati Lseg, gli operatori del mercato monetario stanno già prezzando pienamente un rialzo dei tassi di interesse di 25 punti base entro la fine del 2026. I dati favorevoli sull’inflazione pubblicati a inizio agosto ha però ridotto significativamente le probabilità di un rialzo immediato.

item.title: Irã ameaça 45 petroleiros com multas e confisco em meio a escalada no Estreito de Ormuz
item.description: O Irã afirmou ter colocado na lista negra 45 petroleiros que violaram suas regras para a travessia do Estreito de Ormuz e que tomaria medidas contra quaisquer embarcações que transferissem cargas com eles, intensificando suas ameaças em relação à importante via navegável seis meses após o início da guerra.
item.dc:creator: Nidhi Verma, Florence Tan
item.content:encoded: O Irã afirmou ter colocado na lista negra 45 petroleiros que violaram suas regras para a travessia do Estreito de Ormuz e que tomaria medidas contra quaisquer embarcações que transferissem cargas com eles, intensificando suas ameaças em relação à importante via navegável seis meses após o início da guerra. As embarcações citadas podem ser multadas, detidas e ter suas cargas confiscadas, de acordo com uma publicação no X no final do domingo pela Autoridade do Estreito do Golfo Pérsico, um novo órgão criado pelo Irã para administrar o estreito. A advertência foi emitida poucos dias depois de os EUA terem ameaçado o Irã com “as sanções mais duras da história” e de o Irã ter afirmado que sua resposta a quaisquer novas ameaças dos EUA seria “devastadora”. A lista de restrições inclui superpetroleiros, navios-tanque de gás natural liquefeito e gás de petróleo liquefeito, além de navios de produtos refinados, entre outros. Alguns dos navios citados pertencem à ADNOC Logistics and Shipping (ADNOC L&S) dos Emirados Árabes Unidos, à Navig8 Tankers, subsidiária da ADNOC, e à Bahri, empresa nacional de navegação da Arábia Saudita. Quaisquer embarcações envolvidas em transferências de navio para navio com as embarcações citadas poderiam ser adicionadas à lista negra, acrescentou a publicação iraniana no X. A publicação não especificou o que entendia por “regras do Irã”, mas Teerã já havia afirmado, no passado, que os armadores deveriam obter sua autorização para transitar pelo estreito e que os navios deveriam pagar por serviços de segurança e outros. Os EUA também impuseram um bloqueio naval contra o transporte marítimo relacionado ao Irã. O Golfo fornecia cerca de 20% do petróleo e do gás natural liquefeito diários do mundo antes que o conflito com o Irã interrompesse o tráfego de petroleiros. Esforços coordenados pelos EUA para conduzir petroleiros discretamente pelo Estreito de Ormuz, a fim de abastecer superpetroleiros que aguardam logo fora dele, estão ajudando a restaurar parte desses volumes de exportação. O secretário de Energia dos EUA, Chris Wright, afirmou na sexta-feira no X que “a média de sete dias do petróleo que sai do estreito é superior a 8 milhões de barris por dia. Não se enganem: graças à Marinha dos EUA, o petróleo está fluindo pelo Estreito de Ormuz”. Navios de propriedade da Klaveness Ship Management, da Stolt Tankers e da sul-coreana Sinokor também foram incluídos na lista negra. As empresas de navegação não responderam imediatamente aos pedidos de comentário da Reuters.
